# Product identity, thesis, and goals

## Candidate identity

- Working name: **Engineer Assessment** (`EA-PRODUCT-001`); naming is open.
- Identity: a continuing product offering for engineers and engineering hiring teams. Its identity remains distinct from the `project:ea-research-001` research project, any challenge event, evaluation Method, question bank, model, service, or particular employer deployment.
- Product owner route: `role:ea-product-owner` (role proposed, principal unassigned).
- Candidate posture: `candidate-unadmitted`, authority effect `none`.

## Product thesis

**Problem.** Engineering hiring can consume substantial candidate and team time while using weakly comparable signals. People may be screened by familiarity with conventional interviews rather than the creative, technical and cooperative work a role needs.

**Value mechanism to test.** Three dense cases expose how a candidate generates, analyzes, evaluates, revises, designs, and coordinates decisions. A controlled generator creates comparable but unrehearsed cases; speech-to-text makes evidence inspectable; explicit rubrics and AI-assisted extraction make scoring scalable. Independent validation decides whether the resulting information supports selection.

**Participants and value.** Engineers receive a brief, accessible challenge and actionable evidence-based feedback. Employers may receive a decision aid that saves time and identifies strong future performers. Researchers receive attributable, permissioned observations and reproducible methods. These values are hypotheses until measured.

**First-order constraints.** At most three sessions; at most ten minutes of recorded answer per session; Session 1 centers creativity, analysis and ingenuity through riddles and unusual problems; Session 2 centers technical/product design; Session 3 centers cooperation/communication. Question and score versions are frozen for each administration. Research participation and hiring use have distinct purposes, data rights, and claims.

**Strong thesis.** For one predeclared role, candidate pool, outcome and hiring capacity, the three-session policy meets a predeclared absolute selection-quality target, is non-inferior to the existing longer pipeline, and beats an equal-time comparator on independent later outcomes without unacceptable fairness or access costs. A useful weaker result is incremental improvement when added to a pipeline. Neither result is currently established.

**Revision triggers.** Repeated-form instability, case-family failure, outcome mismatch, subgroup error, participant harm, poor access, or failure in held-out employers changes the thesis or its target scope. A negative result is a research outcome, not a reason to relabel the claim.

## Candidate product capabilities

| ID | Outcome the product must make possible | Evidence gate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| EA-CAP-01 | Engineer completes a versioned three-session assessment within the recorded-time cap. | Usability/access pilot and exact session receipts. |
| EA-CAP-02 | Candidate receives criterion-level feedback linked to answer evidence and uncertainty. | Human review, feedback comprehension, correction test. |
| EA-CAP-03 | Researchers can generate, review, freeze, rotate and retire case families without leaking scored items. | Bank and exposure audit, held-out controls. |
| EA-CAP-04 | Independent scorers can reproduce a score from pinned source, transcript, rubric, and model inputs. | Blind rescore and cold reconstruction. |
| EA-CAP-05 | Researchers can compare the compact policy with longer and equal-time selection methods. | Prospective, preregistered validation run. |
| EA-CAP-06 | Participants can inspect purpose, exercise data rights, and obtain an accessible path. | Rights and accommodation journey review. |
| EA-CAP-07 | Authorized employers can use an accepted, role-specific decision policy only after its gates pass. | Actual owner and legal/use decisions plus current validation. |

Capability descriptions express required outcomes. They do not claim implementation, conformance or adoption.

## Project and goal structure

The Product persists; `project:ea-research-001` coordinates the bounded research and build effort. The goal IDs below are proposed project goals with evidence conditions, not achieved Goal records. Candidate Lab-shaped records for the project and six goals are in [lab-records](lab-records/README.md); `EA-G01` maps to `goal:ea:g01-meaning-ownership`, and likewise through `EA-G06`.

| Goal | Desired result | Acceptance evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| EA-G01 Meaning and ownership | Exact construct, score, claim and authority boundaries are reviewable. | Define v2 Pack, ontology closure, owner review. |
| EA-G02 Case science | The three sessions have reviewed, versioned case families and rubrics. | Item bank, SME review, exposure/quality evals. |
| EA-G03 Reproducible prototype | Consent-based recording, transcription, scoring and feedback work end to end. | Accessible journey, source pins, cold replay, deletion/correction tests. |
| EA-G04 Measurement | Scores are stable enough across cases, raters and response modes for the stated use. | Preregistered reliability, generalizability and subgroup analyses. |
| EA-G05 Predictive claim | Three sessions meet the predeclared selection-quality target against independent outcomes. | Prospective held-out employer/cohort study and independent review. |
| EA-G06 Product decision | Owner decides product posture, claims, market and any hiring use. | Separate signed/reviewed owner and jurisdiction-specific decisions. |

## Claim ladder

`C0 idea` -> `C1 reproducible challenge` -> `C2 reliable narrow construct measure` -> `C3 independent predictive evidence` -> `C4 role-specific selection policy accepted` -> `C5 observed product value`. Each transition requires its own evidence and owner decision. C1 does not imply C2; human/AI agreement does not imply C3; C3 in one role does not imply C4 elsewhere. Current posture is **C0** with an authored proposal and initial literature scan.
